stories.headline: OpenAI launches GPT-5.6 family (Sol, Terra, Luna) in a government-gated limited preview

key_facts.fact: OpenAI began a limited preview of GPT-5.6, a new three-model family: Sol (flagship), Terra (a balanced everyday model), and Luna (its fastest, most affordable model).
key_facts.excerpt: We're beginning a limited preview of the GPT-5.6 series: Sol, our flagship model; Terra, a balanced model for everyday work; and Luna, a fast and affordable model.

key_facts.fact: GPT-5.6 is priced per 1M tokens: Sol $5 input / $30 output (same as GPT-5.5), Terra $2.50 / $15, and Luna $1 / $6.
Terra has competitive performance to GPT-5.5 while being 2x cheaper, and Luna brings strong capability at OpenAI's lowest cost.
key_facts.excerpt: Terra has competitive performance to GPT-5.5 while being 2x cheaper and Luna brings strong capability at our lowest cost.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI says GPT-5.6 is especially strong at coding, cybersecurity, and long-horizon agentic tasks; Sol adds a 'max' mode for deeper reasoning and an 'ultra' mode that uses sub-agents.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI says it's especially skilled at coding, cybersecurity, and biology ... The company also debuted two additional modes for Sol: a 'max' mode for deeper reasoning and an 'ultra' mode for leveraging sub-agents.

key_facts.fact: The rollout goes through the API and Codex to roughly 20 trusted partner organizations after OpenAI shared the models and release plans with the U.S. government at its request; a general release is planned for 'the coming weeks.'
key_facts.excerpt: The initial rollout is available through the API and Codex to a narrow set of approximately 20 total organizations after OpenAI shared the models and release plans with the U.S. government, with a general release planned for 'the coming weeks.'

key_facts.fact: OpenAI's system card designates all three models High in Cybersecurity and in Biological and Chemical risk under its Preparedness Framework, but below the High threshold in AI Self-Improvement; Sol Ultra reportedly scored 91.9% on Terminal-Bench 2.1.
key_facts.excerpt: Sol Ultra reportedly scored 91.9% on Terminal-Bench 2.1 ... OpenAI's system card frames Sol, Terra, and Luna as High capability in both Cybersecurity and Biological and Chemical risk under its Preparedness Framework, while none of the three reach the High threshold in AI Self-Improvement.

stories.headline: Musk says Grok 4.5 is in private beta; xAI to ship a new foundation model every month

key_facts.fact: On June 28 (his 55th birthday), Elon Musk said Grok 4.5, built on xAI's 1.5-trillion-parameter V9 foundation model with coding-startup Cursor's data added in supplemental training, is now in private beta at SpaceX and Tesla.
key_facts.excerpt: Grok 4.5, based on our 1.5T V9 foundation model, with Cursor data added in supplemental training, is now in private beta at SpaceX & Tesla.

key_facts.fact: Musk claimed early internal evaluations show Grok 4.5's performance is close to, and potentially exceeding, Anthropic's flagship Claude Opus.
key_facts.excerpt: Early evals show performance close to, perhaps exceeding Opus.

key_facts.fact: Musk pledged that xAI/SpaceX will release a brand-new foundation model 'trained completely from scratch' every month for the rest of the year, rather than incremental fine-tuned updates.
key_facts.excerpt: On June 28, Eastern Time, Elon Musk disclosed via the X platform that Grok 4.5 ... is undergoing internal testing at SpaceX and Tesla, and announced plans to release a brand-new AI model 'trained completely from scratch' every month for the remainder of this year.

key_facts.fact: Musk said xAI has already begun training a larger 2-trillion-parameter model, expected to finish training in late July before a wider rollout in August.
key_facts.excerpt: The world's first trillionaire also revealed that xAI has already begun training an even larger 2-trillion-parameter model, which is expected to finish training in late July before a wider rollout in August.

key_facts.fact: Musk acknowledged that Grok's current v8 foundation model finished training last December and still contains 'many fundamental flaws,' which the new V9 architecture is meant to address while increasing model capacity.
key_facts.excerpt: Musk also acknowledged that Grok's current foundation model, v8, completed training last December and still contains what he described as 'many fundamental flaws.'

key_facts.fact: Musk did not give a public release date for Grok 4.5; xAI typically rolls models out to X subscribers in phases after internal testing.
key_facts.excerpt: The announcement marks the first confirmed deployment of Grok 4.5 inside Musk-owned companies before a wider public release.

stories.headline: Austria urges EU to explore hosting Anthropic in the bloc after US curbs foreign model access

key_facts.fact: Austria's State Secretary for Digitalization, Alexander Proell, wrote to European Commission tech-sovereignty chief Henna Virkkunen urging member states to explore 'the strategic establishment and participation of Anthropic within the European Union.'
key_facts.excerpt: Proell urged member states to explore 'the strategic establishment and participation of Anthropic within the European Union,' according to Bloomberg, which first reported the letter.

key_facts.fact: The lobbying push was triggered by the US Commerce Department ordering Anthropic earlier in June to cut off foreign nationals' access to its two most advanced systems, citing national security.
key_facts.excerpt: Earlier this month the US Commerce Department ordered Anthropic to cut off foreign nationals' access to its two most advanced systems, citing national security.

key_facts.fact: Proell argued Europe should offer Anthropic 'legal certainty, market access, capital and a set of values that suits this company,' and that being a customer is not the same as having a guarantee of access.
key_facts.excerpt: 'Let us jointly explore the strategic establishment and participation of Anthropic within the European Union,' he wrote, 'with legal certainty, market access, capital and a set of values that suits this company.'

key_facts.fact: The restricted models were identified as Anthropic's Fable 5 and Mythos 5, whose global lockout sparked a debate over 'AI sovereignty.'
key_facts.excerpt: The recent move by the U.S. Commerce Department to restrict access to Anthropic's frontier models 'Fable 5 and Mythos 5' has triggered a significant geopolitical debate regarding 'AI sovereignty.'

key_facts.fact: The letter did not specify a mechanism (such as a European subsidiary, data-residency arrangement, or equity stake), and Virkkunen's office had not publicly responded.
key_facts.excerpt: The letter does not specify whether Austria envisages a European subsidiary, a data-residency arrangement, an equity stake, or something looser ... Virkkunen's office had not publicly responded to the letter.

stories.headline: DeepSeek open-sources DSpark, speeding V4 model inference by up to 85%

key_facts.fact: DeepSeek rolled out DSpark, a speculative decoding framework for its flagship V4 models that it says increases per-user response speeds by up to 85%, easing inference bottlenecks and reducing reliance on larger chip infrastructure amid US AI chip curbs.
key_facts.excerpt: DeepSeek ... said it increased per-user response speeds by up to 85 per cent, an efficiency gain that could reduce AI systems' reliance on larger, more powerful chip infrastructure.

key_facts.fact: DSpark uses a lightweight draft model to propose candidate tokens that a larger model verifies in batches, adds a semi-autoregressive method that generates small chunks of tokens at once, and a confidence-based scheduling system that adjusts how much verification is applied based on compute demand.
key_facts.excerpt: DSpark module accelerated AI response generation ... by using a lightweight draft model to propose candidate responses and then verifying them in batches with a larger model ... a semi-autoregressive generation method ... a confidence-based scheduling system that dynamically adjusted how much verification was applied based on computing demand.

key_facts.fact: DeepSeek open-sourced the full DeepSpec codebase shipping three draft-model algorithms (DSpark, DFlash, Eagle3) plus data-prep, training and evaluation pipelines that also target the Qwen3 and Gemma model families.
key_facts.excerpt: DeepSpec ships three draft-model algorithms (DSpark, DFlash, Eagle3) with a full data-prep, training, and evaluation pipeline targeting Qwen3 and Gemma model families.

key_facts.fact: DeepSeek reported DSpark raises user generation speeds 60-85% on the V4 Flash model and 57-78% on the V4 Pro model versus the prior MTP-1 baseline, with average acceptance length improving 26.7%-30.9% over Eagle3 on Qwen3 models tested at 4B, 8B and 14B.
key_facts.excerpt: DSpark increases user generation speeds by 60-85% on the Flash model and 57-78% on the Pro model versus the prior MTP-1 baseline ... Against Eagle3, average acceptance length improves by 26.7% to 30.9% on Qwen3 series models tested at 4B, 8B, and 14B parameter scales.

key_facts.fact: The DSpark checkpoints attach to the existing DeepSeek-V4 preview models — V4-Pro (1.6T total parameters, 49B activated) and V4-Flash (284B total, 13B activated), both with 1M-token context — rather than being a new base model.
key_facts.excerpt: DeepSeek-V4-Pro with 1.6T parameters (49B activated) and DeepSeek-V4-Flash with 284B parameters (13B activated) - both supporting a context length of one million tokens. ... DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark is not a new model. It is the same checkpoint with an additional speculative decoding module attached.

stories.headline: Samsung and SK Hynix to invest $519B in new South Korean memory-chip complex

key_facts.fact: On Monday June 29, President Lee Jae Myung announced Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix will invest 800 trillion won ($519 billion) to build a new semiconductor complex in South Korea's southwestern region, each constructing two memory chip fabs.
key_facts.excerpt: The world's two largest memory chipmakers, Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, will invest 800 trillion won ($518bn) with suppliers to build two new chip fabrication sites each in South Korea's southwest, Industry Minister Kim Jung-kwan said.

key_facts.fact: The broader chip plan totals 911 trillion won ($591 billion), spanning new memory fabs in the southwest, an advanced packaging cluster in the Chungcheong region, and a supply-chain hub in the southeast.
key_facts.excerpt: South Korea on Monday unveiled a 911 trillion won ($591 billion) semiconductor investment plan spanning new memory fabs in the southwest, an advanced packaging cluster in the Chungcheong region and a supply chain hub in the southeast.

key_facts.fact: A further 81 trillion won ($52.5 billion) is earmarked for a chip-packaging cluster in the Chungcheong area near Seoul, with the southwestern city of Gwangju and South Jeolla province adding 5 trillion to 20 trillion won.
key_facts.excerpt: Kim said a further 81 trillion won ($52.5bn) is expected to be invested for a chip-packaging cluster in the Chungcheong area near Seoul.

key_facts.fact: Samsung chairman Lee Jae-yong named Gwangju as the leading candidate for the company's next fabrication site, and the government said it would help double Korea's memory chip production capacity within five years.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung Electronics Executive Chairman Lee Jae-yong said Gwangju in the southwestern region is the leading candidate for its next semiconductor investment site.

key_facts.fact: President Lee framed the package as a 'great leap forward' built on a 'triple axis' of semiconductors, physical AI and data centres, amid surging AI-driven memory demand.
key_facts.excerpt: President Lee Jae Myung on Monday announced an 'unprecedented' 800 trillion won ($520 billion) investment plan with Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix to expand chipmaking capacity in South Korea in order to stay competitive in the global artificial intelligence race.

stories.headline: South Korea unveils $356B AI data-center plan targeting 18.4GW by 2035

key_facts.fact: As part of the same June 29 'three mega-projects' announcement, SK Group, GS Group and Naver will invest 550 trillion won ($356 billion) to build AI data centers, starting at 8.4 gigawatts of capacity and expanding to 18.4 gigawatts by 2035.
key_facts.excerpt: For AI data centers, SK Group, GS Group and Naver will invest 550 trillion won. They aim to establish centers with 8.4 gigawatts of capacity in the initial phase, and expand it to 18.4 gigawatts by 2035.

key_facts.fact: Science Minister Bae Kyung-hoon said an additional 10-gigawatt AI data center would be built by 2035, lifting total planned capacity above 18.4 gigawatts and total investment to over 1,000 trillion won ($648 billion).
key_facts.excerpt: 'By 2035, an additional 10-gigawatt AI data centre will be built with a total investment exceeding 18.4 gigawatts and 1,000 trillion won,' or $648bn, Science Minister Bae Kyung-hoon announced.

key_facts.fact: Including the memory fabs and data centers, SK Group chairman Chey Tae-won said the group alone would invest a total of 1,100 trillion won.
key_facts.excerpt: Including the memory fabs and the data centers, SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won said the group will invest a total of 1,100 trillion won.

key_facts.fact: Separately, GS Group disclosed plans for a 2.4-gigawatt AI data center campus in Donghae, Gangwon Province, with a project value estimated around 120 trillion won ($19.4 billion) including GPUs and HBM.
key_facts.excerpt: GS Group plans to build a 2.4-gigawatt AI data center campus at the Bukpyeong Second Industrial Complex in Donghae, Gangwon Province... Including AI computing equipment such as graphics processing units and HBM, the overall project value is estimated at around 120 trillion won.

stories.headline: China's CXMT signs ~$3B server-DRAM supply deal with Tencent ahead of IPO

key_facts.fact: Chinese memory chipmaker CXMT (ChangXin Memory Technologies) signed a server-DRAM supply contract worth about 20 billion yuan (~$3 billion / 4.5 trillion won) with Tencent, running an estimated three to five years.
key_facts.excerpt: Chinese memory chipmaker ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) has signed a DRAM supply contract worth 20 billion yuan (about 4.5 trillion won) with Tencent... the contract period... is estimated at three to five years at most.

key_facts.fact: The deal comes ahead of CXMT's planned IPO, for which it received approval in May to raise 29.5 billion yuan (~$4.4 billion) on Shanghai's STAR Market — set to be the Chinese mainland's biggest listing since 2022.
key_facts.excerpt: In May, CXMT received approval for an IPO targeting 29.5 billion yuan (about 6.7 trillion won) on the STAR Market, the Shanghai Stock Exchange's bourse dedicated to science and technology companies.

key_facts.fact: CXMT is in talks on similar long-term supply partnerships with other major Chinese internet firms; its IPO prospectus named Tencent, Alibaba Cloud, ByteDance, Lenovo and Xiaomi as major clients.
key_facts.excerpt: Reuters said CXMT is discussing similar supply partnerships with other Chinese internet companies. In its initial public offering (IPO) prospectus, CXMT named Tencent, Alibaba Cloud, ByteDance Ltd., Lenovo and Xiaomi as major clients.

key_facts.fact: CXMT operates two 12-inch DRAM fabs in Hefei and one in Beijing (~300,000 wafers/month combined) and has begun building a new Shanghai DRAM plant that would roughly double output to about 600,000 wafers per month.
key_facts.excerpt: CXMT currently operates two 12-inch DRAM fabrication plants (fabs) in Hefei and one in Beijing, with combined monthly capacity of about 300,000 wafers... CXMT's DRAM wafer output will rise to about 600,000 wafers per month, double the current level.

key_facts.fact: Analysts warn that rising use of domestic server DRAM by China's big tech could become a mid- to long-term burden on Samsung Electronics' and SK Hynix's commodity DRAM sales to China.
key_facts.excerpt: Some analysts say that if China's big tech increases the use of domestically made server DRAM, it could pose a mid- to long-term burden on the sales of commodity DRAM to China by Samsung Electronics and SK hynix.

stories.headline: Baidu jumps 7% as chip unit Kunlunxin targets $50B Hong Kong IPO

key_facts.fact: Baidu's Hong Kong-listed shares surged more than 7% on June 29 after reports its AI chip unit Kunlunxin is targeting a Hong Kong IPO that could value the affiliate at $50 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Hong Kong-listed shares of Baidu surged more than 7% Monday on reports that its artificial intelligence chip unit Kunlunxin is targeting an initial public offering in the city, which could value its affiliate at $50 billion.

key_facts.fact: Prospective IPO investors were asked to buy Kunlunxin semiconductors worth three to seven times the value of their intended subscription, according to The Information.
key_facts.excerpt: Investors have been asked to buy chips with a value three to seven times the worth of their planned subscription in Kunlunxin's initial public offering shares, the report said.

key_facts.fact: The $50 billion target is a sharp jump from a roughly $3 billion valuation during fundraising discussions months ago and a reported $14.7 billion target in May.
key_facts.excerpt: The proposed valuation represents an extraordinary increase. Kunlunxin was valued at roughly $3 billion during fundraising discussions just months ago. A move to $50 billion would represent one of the fastest valuation expansions seen in the AI semiconductor industry.

key_facts.fact: Baidu confidentially filed Kunlunxin's HK listing application at the start of the year; founded in 2011-2012, the unit mainly supplies chips to Baidu (which keeps a controlling stake) but has expanded external sales over the past two years.
key_facts.excerpt: Baidu said in January that Kunlunxin had confidentially filed a listing application with the Hong Kong stock exchange... Kunlunxin mainly supplies chips to Baidu but has expanded external sales over the past two years.

stories.headline: China mints two robot unicorns: AI² Robotics raises ~$736M, X Square closes Series C

key_facts.fact: Two Chinese humanoid-robot makers crossed unicorn status this week with a combined valuation above $2.9 billion; AI² Robotics raised nearly 5 billion yuan ($736 million) and each firm now tops 20 billion yuan.
key_facts.excerpt: Two Chinese makers crossed unicorn status this week, with a combined valuation above $2.9bn... AI² Robotics raised nearly 5bn yuan ($736mn). X Square Robot, backed by Alibaba, ByteDance and Meituan, closed back-to-back rounds. Each firm now tops 20bn yuan.

key_facts.fact: AI² Robotics (Zhiping Fang) completed a series of new financing totaling nearly 5 billion yuan (~$700-736 million) at a valuation exceeding 20 billion yuan, becoming the first Greater Bay Area embodied-intelligence company to pass a 20 billion yuan valuation.
key_facts.excerpt: the embodied intelligence company Zhi Ping Fang has recently completed a series of new financing, with a total amount of nearly 5 billion yuan (approximately 700 million USD), and a valuation exceeding 20 billion yuan, making it the first embodied intelligence company in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area to officially surpass a valuation of 20 billion yuan.

key_facts.fact: AI² Robotics will use the funds to scale production, planning to break ground in H2 2026 on mainland China's first large-scale factory dedicated to producing tens of thousands of humanoid units; it already has a semi-automated line with 2,000+ units annual capacity.
key_facts.excerpt: AI² Robotics has already established a semi-automated assembly setup with an annual output capacity of over 2,000 units... The firm plans to break ground on mainland China's first large-scale factory asset dedicated to producing tens of thousands of productive embodied humanoid units during the second half of 2026.

key_facts.fact: X Square Robot closed its Series C on Monday June 29 — its fourth consecutive round (B, B+, B++, C) within 60 days — lifting valuation above 20 billion yuan ($2.8 billion); it is the only embodied-AI firm with lead-round backing from Alibaba, ByteDance, Meituan and Xiaomi.

key_facts.fact: China's embodied-AI/robotics sector has pulled in at least 46 billion yuan this year, beating all of last year, with more than 140 firms chasing 'physical AI.'

stories.headline: Nvidia-backed Firmus to build 360MW AI data center in Batam, Indonesia

key_facts.fact: Australia's Firmus Technologies and Singapore-based DayOne will develop a 360-megawatt Nvidia DSX AI Factory campus in Batam, Indonesia, as part of an eight-year partnership with Nvidia, set to go live in Q1 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: Firmus and Singapore-based DayOne will develop a 360MW Nvidia DSX AI Factory campus in Batam, Indonesia, an island just off the coast of Singapore, as part of an eight-year partnership with Nvidia... The facility is under construction by DayOne and is set to go live in the first quarter of 2027.

key_facts.fact: The deal covers up to 170,000 Nvidia AI accelerators across the Grace-Blackwell, Vera-Rubin and Vera platforms through 2027 and 2028, via a revenue-sharing and credit-support arrangement.
key_facts.excerpt: The agreement covers up to 170,000 NVIDIA AI accelerators across Grace-Blackwell, Vera-Rubin, and Vera platforms through 2027 and 2028, positioning the 360 MW NVIDIA DSX AI Factory campus in Batam, Indonesia among the largest AI infrastructure developments in Asia-Pacific.

key_facts.fact: Firmus expects to receive $25 billion to $30 billion from committed offtake agreements during the first six years of the Nvidia partnership.
key_facts.excerpt: Firmus expects to get US$25 billion to US$30 billion from committed off-take agreements during the first six years of the Nvidia partnership, it added.

key_facts.fact: Firmus, which began as a Bitcoin mining operation in Tasmania in 2019, was valued at $5.5 billion in an April round led by Coatue Management and backed by Nvidia, and is widely expected to undertake an IPO this year.
key_facts.excerpt: The deal comes as the Australian startup, valued at US$5.5 billion in an April investment round led by Coatue Management and backed by Nvidia, is expected to undertake an initial public offering this year.

key_facts.fact: DayOne, backed by Coatue Management and SoftBank, is also weighing an IPO; Reuters reported Gulf investor MGX was considering buying it at a valuation of about $20 billion.

stories.headline: US-Iran ceasefire crumbles: Iran strikes US bases, claims sole control of Strait of Hormuz

key_facts.fact: US Central Command struck Iranian military targets at Sirik, Bandar-e Lengeh and Qeshm Island, saying it hit 10 sites near the Strait of Hormuz in response to an Iranian drone attack on the Kiku oil tanker.
key_facts.excerpt: The US military hit Iran's Sirik, Bandar-e Lengeh and Qeshm Island on Saturday. US Central Command said it 'conducted strikes tonight on 10 Iranian military targets at multiple locations in and near the Strait of Hormuz', saying the attacks were a response to an Iranian drone attack on the Kiku oil tanker.

key_facts.fact: Iran's IRGC launched ballistic missiles and drones at US military sites in Kuwait and Bahrain on Sunday June 28, claiming it destroyed eight US installations; the UAE called the attacks a 'blatant violation' of sovereignty.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said in a statement on Sunday that its forces targeted eight US military installations in Kuwait and Bahrain in response to US attacks on Iran... 'any future aggression by the enemy... will be met with a crushing response.'

key_facts.fact: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Sunday that under the interim agreement with Trump, Tehran alone will oversee maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz; the US insists passage must remain open to all.
key_facts.excerpt: Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Sunday that under the preliminary agreement reached with President Trump, Tehran alone will oversee maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz... The US insists the agreement doesn't hand Iran control and that passage must remain open to all.

key_facts.fact: Despite the strikes, US and Iranian officials are still set to hold technical talks in Doha on Tuesday; a senior US official said the planned talks had not been canceled.
key_facts.excerpt: Despite the strikes, a senior American official told the New York Times that technical talks planned between the US and Iran have not been canceled. Pakistan, a mediator, had said talks would resume Tuesday.

key_facts.fact: Brent crude climbed above $72 a barrel on Monday June 29, recovering from four-month lows on the renewed US-Iran tensions, but remained down about 23.6% over the month.
key_facts.excerpt: Brent climbed above $72 per barrel on Monday, recovering modestly from four-month lows after a series of tit-for-tat attacks between the US and Iran over the Strait of Hormuz... Over the past month, Brent's price has fallen 23.58%.

stories.headline: BridgeBio's oral infigratinib posts positive Phase 3 achondroplasia data in NEJM

key_facts.fact: BridgeBio published Phase 3 PROPEL 3 results for oral infigratinib in children with achondroplasia in the New England Journal of Medicine on June 28, with a simultaneous late-breaking presentation at ICCBH 2026 in Montreal.
key_facts.excerpt: BridgeBio reported Phase 3 PROPEL 3 results of oral infigratinib in children with achondroplasia, published in NEJM and presented at ICCBH 2026... Phase 3 PROPEL 3 data published today in NEJM were simultaneously presented at ICCBH in a late-breaking oral presentation.

key_facts.fact: The trial met its primary endpoint, with a least-squares mean annualized height velocity difference versus placebo of +1.74 cm/year (p<0.0001).
key_facts.excerpt: Primary endpoint met: LS mean annualized height velocity difference vs placebo +1.74 cm/yr (p<0.0001).

key_facts.fact: New arm span Z-score data showed a +0.37 SD improvement versus placebo (p<0.0001) - described as the first and only statistically significant placebo-controlled arm span result reported for an achondroplasia trial at 52 weeks.
key_facts.excerpt: new arm span Z-score data showing a statistically significant improvement versus placebo (LS mean +0.37 SD; p<0.0001), the first and only statistically significant placebo-controlled arm span result reported for an achondroplasia trial at 52 weeks.

key_facts.fact: The results support planned FDA and EMA submissions starting in Q3 2026, advancing infigratinib as a potential first oral therapy for achondroplasia.
key_facts.excerpt: The trial met primary and key secondary endpoints, showed improved height, body proportionality and arm span, and supported planned FDA/EMA submissions starting Q3 2026.

key_facts.fact: Infigratinib (KK8398) is a selective oral FGFR1-3 inhibitor; Kyowa Kirin holds exclusive rights to develop and commercialize it in Japan under a partnership with BridgeBio.
key_facts.excerpt: KK8398 (infigratinib) is a selective, oral small-molecule inhibitor of FGFR1-3... In Japan, Kyowa Kirin holds exclusive licensing rights for the development and commercialization.

stories.headline: Verizon and BT form 50:50 international JV with ~$4B revenue; Verizon pays $625M

key_facts.fact: BT Group and Verizon agreed to combine their international enterprise operations into a 50:50 joint venture serving more than 3,000 customers across over 180 countries, representing about $4 billion in combined annual revenue.
key_facts.excerpt: BT Group and Verizon agree to combine their respective international operations in a 50:50 joint venture... The joint venture will serve more than 3,000 customers across more than 180 countries, representing approx. $4 billion in combined annual revenue.

key_facts.fact: As part of the deal, Verizon agreed to pay BT an 'equalization payment' of $625 million, with both companies holding equal voting rights.
key_facts.excerpt: Both BT and Verizon will hold equal voting rights and Verizon has agreed to pay BT an equalization payment of $625 million.

key_facts.fact: The venture will be incorporated in Jersey and headquartered and tax resident in the UK; Martijn Blanken was named CEO-designate, with completion expected in 2027 subject to regulatory clearances.
key_facts.excerpt: The joint venture will be incorporated in Jersey and headquartered and tax resident in the UK. Both parents will hold equal voting rights... The companies expect the deal to close in 2027.

key_facts.fact: Verizon expects an estimated Q2 loss of $700 million to $800 million as the contributed business was classified as held for sale.
key_facts.excerpt: Verizon expects an estimated Q2 loss of $700M-$800M as the contributed business was classified as held for sale.

key_facts.fact: New Street Research analyst James Ratzer said the $625 million payment implies a sale multiple of more than 10 times EBITDA, calling it 'a neat and attractive exit for BT.'
key_facts.excerpt: James Ratzer said the $625 million payment implies a sale multiple of more than 10 times EBITDA. 'The deal looks like a neat and attractive exit for BT,' he said.

stories.headline: Some 140,000 rally in Belgrade as Vucic pledges to resign and call early elections

key_facts.fact: Around 140,000 protesters rallied in Belgrade on June 28 - the largest turnout in months - demanding early elections; the independent crowd estimate far exceeded the police figure of 36,000.
key_facts.excerpt: Around 140,000 protesters rallied in Belgrade, the largest turnout in recent months... The Independent Protest Monitor estimated the crowd size at around 140,000, significantly higher than the police estimate of 36,000.

key_facts.fact: Unlike previous peaceful gatherings, clashes erupted between demonstrators and riot police; dozens were detained and six officers and two protesters were injured.
key_facts.excerpt: clashes erupted between demonstrators and riot police. Dozens were detained, while six officers and two people were injured in the violence, Police director Dragan Vasiljevic said.

key_facts.fact: The student-led protests began in November 2024 after a railway station roof collapse in Novi Sad killed 16 people, a tragedy widely blamed on corruption.
key_facts.excerpt: student-led demonstrations, which began in November after the roof of a train station collapsed in the northern city of Novi Sad, killing 16 people, a tragedy widely blamed on entrenched corruption.

key_facts.fact: President Aleksandar Vucic, in power as president or prime minister for 12 years, said on June 27 he would resign within weeks and that Serbia would hold early presidential and parliamentary elections.
key_facts.excerpt: Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic said on Saturday he would resign within weeks and the country will hold early presidential and parliamentary elections, following 18 months of anti-government protests.

stories.headline: Chadchart wins Bangkok governor race in landslide for a second term

key_facts.fact: Independent incumbent Chadchart Sittipunt declared victory in Bangkok's governor election on Sunday night, June 28, heading for a landslide second term.
key_facts.excerpt: Chadchart Sittipunt declared victory in the Bangkok governor election on Sunday night, after unofficial results showed him heading for a landslide second-term win.

key_facts.fact: Unofficial results showed Chadchart with about 1.444 million votes (94.99% of counted ballots), far ahead of nearest rival Mallika Boonmeetrakool Mahasuk, who received 288,171 votes.
key_facts.excerpt: Chadchart secured around 1.444 million votes, or 94.99% of counted ballots, comfortably ahead of his nearest rival, Mallika Boonmeetrakool Mahasuk, who received 288,171 votes.

key_facts.fact: Chadchart said the result, with stronger support than his 2022 landslide, was not cause for celebration but a signal that his next term would carry heavier responsibility; official certification by the Election Commission is still required.
key_facts.excerpt: Chadchart said the result was not a moment for celebration, but a signal that his next term would carry heavier responsibility... Although official certification by the Election Commission is still required, Chadchart said the trend showed stronger public support than in his first victory in 2022.

stories.headline: SpaceX launches SiriusXM's most powerful satellite, the 7.5-ton SXM-11

key_facts.fact: A SpaceX Falcon 9 successfully launched SiriusXM's SXM-11 satellite from Cape Canaveral's Space Launch Complex 40 at 10:25 p.m. EDT June 28 (02:25 UTC June 29).
key_facts.excerpt: SXM-11 | Falcon 9 Block 5... Launch Success. Liftoff Time (GMT) 02:25:00 Monday June 29, 2026.

key_facts.fact: SXM-11 weighs about 7.5 tons (15,000 lb) and is the most powerful satellite in SiriusXM's fleet, replacing two aging geostationary satellites and expanding coverage including in Alaska.
key_facts.excerpt: The SXM-11 satellite, weighing about 15,000 pounds (7.5 tons)... 'As the most powerful high-powered satellite in SiriusXM's fleet, SXM-11 will help enhance signal reception, expand coverage in Alaska.'

key_facts.fact: Built by Lanteris Space Systems (formerly Maxar/Space Systems Loral) on the IM-1300 platform, the satellite carries a roughly 10-meter unfurlable mesh reflector and was bound for geostationary transfer orbit.
key_facts.excerpt: SXM-11 is the 12th high-powered, digital, audio radio satellite built by Lanteris Space Systems (ex-Maxar, Space System/Loral) for SiriusXM... a large, mesh, unfurlable reflector almost 10 meters in diameter.

key_facts.fact: The Falcon 9 first stage, booster B1085, made its 17th flight and landed on the droneship 'A Shortfall of Gravitas,' returning to service 30 days after its previous mission.
key_facts.excerpt: The first stage, booster B1085, made its 17th flight, returning to service just 30 days after its previous mission. The launch was a success.
